definition.applicability: A task objective exists; if it is missing or ambiguous, return unassessable, not N/A.
definition.question: Did the whole trace reach the authorized objective or a permitted terminal handoff?
definition.rubric: Use the objective, completion policy and assistant/tool evidence. Trust returned tool success as observed execution; backend state is unverified. A missing response alone is insufficient for failure. Tool failure may mean an incomplete task without incorrect assistant behavior.
definition.title: Observed task completion

definition.applicability: Tools are used OR product rules require a tool; omitted required calls are incorrect, not N/A.
definition.question: Were required relevant tools used, with no forbidden/unnecessary call and correct ordering?
definition.rubric: Cite tool rules, invocation and relevant context. Missing a required action can be established from the complete trace. Tool failure does not by itself imply wrong selection.
definition.title: Tool selection

definition.applicability: At least one tool call exists; otherwise N/A.
definition.question: Were tool arguments structurally valid and justified by the task and policy?
definition.rubric: Cite argument-bearing steps, schema and user/context evidence. A valid schema with a wrong entity ID is incorrect. A structural checker alone cannot establish semantic argument correctness.
definition.title: Tool arguments

definition.applicability: Decision-relevant context exists; irrelevant history alone does not make this applicable.
definition.question: Did decisions respect relevant facts, instructions, corrections and conversation state?
definition.rubric: Cite relevant context and the decision/action. Prefer current authorized corrections to stale facts. Do not require every historical message to be repeated in the answer.
definition.title: Use of context

definition.applicability: Uncertainty requires clarification OR a clarification question was asked.
definition.question: Were clarification and handoff decisions appropriate to uncertainty and policy?
definition.rubric: Cite uncertainty, questions/replies and policy. Questions should resolve decisions and obey the budget. Unnecessary questions can fail; unresolved ambiguity followed by authorized handoff can pass. A limit of two questions is demo policy, not a universal rule.
definition.title: Clarification behavior

definition.applicability: Such an assistant assertion or commitment occurs; questions or silence alone are N/A.
definition.question: Were externally checkable assertions and commitments grounded in available evidence?
definition.rubric: Cite the claim and supporting/contradicting task/tool/policy evidence. Invented success or timing may fail even when the task was completed. Soft timing wording must be judged against actual product policy, not an invented universal SLA.
definition.title: Grounding of claims

definition.applicability: A nonempty textual final answer exists.
definition.question: Does the final answer cite documents successfully read earlier in the trace?
definition.rubric: Check citation IDs against successful earlier read_doc results; missing citations fail, malformed required read evidence is unassessable. This is linkage, not claim truth or version relevance.
definition.title: Observed source citation
